why: Instrument defect found while building, before any measured run: the planted sidecar's output was an absolute scratch path, but holon.frontends.solidity's sidecar check requires a repo-relative path ending .extracted.json, so every extraction was refused before the walker ran and the three budget tests could hold under no implementation. The output is now the repo-relative tests_m6/fixtures/i109/sol/wide.extracted.json (the test passes --out, so nothing is written there). The budgets (5, 4000000, none), the contract and every assertion are unchanged.

Instrument defect found while building, before any measured run: the test passed the fixture directory tests_m6/fixtures/i109/sol as --source, but holon.frontends.solidity refuses a source tree that is not its own clean git checkout (the frontend records the checkout's commit), so every extraction was refused before the walker ran and the budget tests could hold under no implementation. The test now copies the fixture into its scratch directory and commits it there (git init, add, commit) and passes that checkout. The fixture, the budgets and every assertion are unchanged.

Instrument defect found while building, before any measured run (the third of this helper pair): holon.frontends.solidity refuses a sidecar whose target.commit is not the checkout's HEAD, and the planted sidecar named 40 zeros, so every extraction was refused before the walker ran. _side takes the commit (default unchanged) and _extract passes the scratch checkout's HEAD. The budgets, the contract and every assertion are unchanged.

Instrument defect found while building, before any measured run: as the amendment of _side states, the sidecar must name the scratch checkout's HEAD, so _extract now commits the fixture first, reads HEAD and writes the sidecar after. The budgets, the contract and every assertion are unchanged.

Instrument defect found while building, before any measured run: the test looked for the whole-write refusal in the source of holon.sorts.model3.Gen, but the write compiler (write_body) is a method of its subclass Machine(Gen), so the text was never in the inspected source and the test could hold under no implementation. It now inspects model3.Machine.write_body, where the refusal 'a write of a whole <label>' is raised. The claim (A4: a whole-map write stays refused) is unchanged.

Instrument defect found while building, before any measured run: the test asked that s<(trunc(64, x), 10) get a sign other than '?', equal to the unsigned <'s. But D9 gives the unsigned <(trunc(64, x), 10) the sign '?' itself (a truncation wraps, so it is not monotone in x), so the two could only be equal at '?' and the test could hold under no sound implementation. The operand is now the register read x itself, with x in SG1's narrow set (declared uint64, bool or address: every read below 2^255), passed as sign's new narrow argument; the test also checks that without the declaration the same comparison stays '?'. The rule (SG1: operands provably below 2^255 take the unsigned sign) and the other tests are unchanged.
